Theme

Work & responsibility

deadline noun

also due date, time limit, set a deadline

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.1.148: diem praestituit operī faciundō (Lewis & Short)

diēs praestitūta

phrase: diēs, feminine of a fixed day, with the participle of praestituere

the day fixed beforehand

Lewis & Short: praestituere, to determine or appoint beforehand; to set a deadline is diem praestituere. Diēs is feminine of a day fixed or appointed.

Other words

  • diēs praescrīptus — the prescribed day

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. deadline, after Erasmus, Colloquia: ad diem praescrīptum

Examples

  • diem praestituit operī faciundō

    he set a deadline for doing the workCic. Verr. 2.1.148

See also schedule, complete.

SourcesLewis & Short: praestituo · Lewis & Short: praescribo · Lewis & Short: dies

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. deadline.
